overview: After 1.e4 Nc6 White plays 2.b4, offering the b-pawn so Black's knight is pulled away. After 2...Nxb4 3.c3 Nc6 4.d4 White has a big centre for the pawn and Black's knight has lost two tempi. Black can also play 2...e5 3.b5 Nce7 and keep the pawn structure.

white_ideas.idea: Build a big centre with c3 and d4

black_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn and consolidate with ...d5 or ...e5
Return the pawn at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on c3, d4, e4 against Black knight on c6

character.notes: White sacrifices a pawn for centre and tempo; both sides have chances.

gambit.notes: After 2...Nxb4 White is a pawn down and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious; Black can keep the pawn with accurate play.

structure.notes: Open centre with c3 and d4.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black declines and keeps the structure

character.reason: White gambits a pawn for centre.

gambit.reason: White gives the b-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: White gets too little for the pawn.
